sources.title: SQLite transaction control
sources.version: Current SQLite documentation; no release pin
sources.locator: Transactions §2.1–2.2; DEFERRED/IMMEDIATE and SQLITE_BUSY
sources.access_utc: 2026-10-12T00:39:51Z (clock immediately before the open batch; page fetch followed in the same call)
sources.observed_operation: Opened official transaction documentation; read writer concurrency, deferred upgrade, immediate-lock, and busy conditions.
sources.condition: Default transactions are DEFERRED; multiple readers are allowed but only one write transaction at a time. BEGIN IMMEDIATE begins a write transaction immediately and can return SQLITE_BUSY when another writer is active.
sources.applicability: Single-host booking authority; acquire the write reservation before availability check and handle busy/conflict outcomes.

sources.access_utc: 2026-10-12T00:39:51Z (clock immediately before the open batch; page fetch followed in the same call)
sources.observed_operation: Opened official WAL documentation; read host restriction, one-writer constraint, backup sidecar warning, checkpoint behavior, and WAL-reset fix note.
sources.condition: WAL allows reader/writer overlap but only one writer; all DB processes must run on same host and WAL does not work over network filesystems. WAL-reset corruption bug is described as fixed in 3.51.3 and backported to 3.50.7 and 3.44.6.
sources.applicability: Keep SQLite and its application on one host; use supported fixed runtime for WAL; do not share its DB file across LAN/NFS.
